rows.sourced_today: Saint-Gobain Hexoloy SA 4-point flexural strength 380 MPa on a 3 x 4 x 45 mm bar. Compressive strength on the same sheets is 3900 MPa.
rows.weibull_note: Two-parameter Weibull at P_f = 0.001, m = 10, sigma_0 taken as 380 MPa, same volume as the bar. m = 10 is the seal-tube and structural-tile page. Sheet B-1003-2 lists 8 for standard SA and 12 for enhanced SA. This is not a volume-scaled tube allowable, and it is not a compression test.
rows.state: PENDING-025. 380 and 3900 exist on the datasheet. The 190 MPa figure is a calculation. This card carries 3900 MPa as 011b did. Using it as a tube allowable is an optimism. MAINLINE-025 owns the row.

rows.note: PENDING-025. At the sourced-today point the axial stress is the contact stress if the tube section bears the member force. Perry is the scored bending-imperfection mode. MAINLINE-025 owns the allowable.

rows.exists: Hexoloy SA process tubes: OD 25 to 381 mm, single piece to 1.4 m, bonded assemblies to 4.9 m. Seal tubes are about 0.30 m long. Silit SiSiC radiant tubes reach OD 300 mm, length 3.5 m, thinnest published wall about 4 mm, Amasic-3D about 2 mm.
rows.state: PENDING-025. A 250 mm class diameter exists. A 2 m single Hexoloy piece does not. A wall near 0.9 mm is below the 2 mm SiSiC floor and is a PROJECTION for alpha-SiC. MAINLINE-025 owns the manufacture row. These factors are context at the sourced-today geometry, not a closed finding.
rows.source: https://www.ceramicsrefractories.saint-gobain.com/products/shapes/tubes/hexoloy-sic-process-tubes and the ceramic radiant tube page

rows.state: PENDING-023. This card carries joints at 5 percent of film, nodes and tubes, 216.427144889 kg. The bounds are context only: a SiC pad at 380 MPa over one tube diameter of engagement. MAINLINE-023 owns the joint mass. A 1 MN ceramic load introduction is not a catalog fitting.

rows.today: Mylar 850H, tensile MD 22 kpsi, density 1.40 g/cc, O2 transmission 6.0 cc/100 in2/day at 48 gauge and 1 atm.
rows.method: MAINLINE-016: 1 percent of lift per day is 48.894 kg, and permeance is converted as scc to mol to kg at p_ext. Mylar transmission is scaled as 1/thickness from the 48-gauge line.
rows.projection: The 011 film, 1.5 GPa at 970 kg/m3, has no datasheet. It is the film optimism.
rows.state: PENDING-024. This card carries the 011b film: 1.5 GPa, 970 kg/m3. Mylar exists and is the sourced-today comparison. The 1.5 GPa film is a PROJECTION. MAINLINE-024 owns the film, its thickness and the vacuum permeation. Seams are not in the Mylar figure.

rows.recommendation: Use k 0.2 for ceramic arcs. A brittle member does not shed load after first crack. Wright 1965 used a modified k of 0.4 for a reticulated-shell table. That factor is an optimism here.
rows.state: Both values are in the catalog. k 0.2 is the brief's band floor.

rows.note: MAINLINE-021 has filed (rpt-ref-fe49179fb6a8ad8c986e). Its P2 sandwich reaches SF 1 on gamma 2.90 times 0.20 and a wrinkling coefficient 1.10 times 0.33, at a face allowable of 283 MPa. Least mode 1.000. Full named set 1.111. This frame's least equilateral set is arc_rise_above_sphere, least SF 1.35387562843. The P2 sandwich needs less optimism. Its largest named factor is 2.90, and this frame's largest is 8 (arc rise over the spherical sagitta, factor 8). Both are QUESTIONABLE.

This card keeps 011b's E of 410 GPa and density 3100 kg/m3 so the regression is the same material. Hexoloy pages also print E 430 GPa, density 3.10 to 3.15 g/cm3, and Poisson's ratio 0.14. The local-buckling coefficient stays 0.6.
